steps.say: Reactive arthritis is sterile joint inflammation that follows gut or genital infection by 1 to 4 weeks. Salmonella, Shigella, Yersinia, Campylobacter, and Chlamydia are the triggers. This figure is the display of the triad and skin lesions. Antibiotics are for the trigger, not the arthritis.
steps.tx: A hot joint that follows dysentery or urethral discharge by weeks is reactive arthritis: acute sterile inflammatory **synovitis** (joint inflammation without live organisms) beginning **1 to 4 weeks** after a distant gut or genital infection. The bowel culprits are **Salmonella** enterica, Shigella flexneri, Yersinia enterocolitica, and Campylobacter jejuni, while genital cases trace to **Chlamydia** trachomatis. Synovial cultures are sterile by definition, which is what separates this arthritis from septic joints.

vis.alt: Clinical manifestations of reactive arthritis including the classic triad and mucocutaneous lesions.
vis.caption: Sterile arthritis follows infection by weeks with urethritis, eye inflammation, and joint swelling. Cultures are sterile by definition. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: HLA-B27 is present in 60 to 85 percent of patients. Positivity is the predictor of severe, axial, and chronic disease with skin lesions. Negative patients usually have a milder self limited course. Every patient requires one HLA-B27 test.
steps.tx: **HLA-B27** (the spondylitis tissue type) is present in **60 to 85 percent** of reactive arthritis patients. Positivity predicts greater severity, axial involvement, chronic relapses, and widespread mucocutaneous disease. HLA-B27 negative patients usually run a milder self limited course. A positive test indicates prolonged follow up, while a negative test reassures toward resolution.

steps.say: The triad is urethritis, conjunctivitis, and asymmetric arthritis of large lower limb joints. The brunt falls on knees, ankles, and subtalar joints. The full triad is present in a minority. Two of three with a trigger is enough for the diagnosis.
steps.tx: The classical triad, once called **Reiter syndrome**, combines non-gonococcal urethritis or cervicitis with **conjunctivitis** (eye surface inflammation) and acute asymmetric oligoarthritis of large weight bearing lower limb joints such as knees, ankles, and subtalar joints. The complete triad appears in a minority, so two features with a proven trigger are enough. A knee effusion with red eyes weeks after enteritis is reactive arthritis until proven otherwise.

steps.say: Skin lesions clinch the diagnosis when joints are equivocal. Keratoderma gives pustular papules, on palms and soles. Circinate balanitis is painless, serpiginous erosion of the glans. Both are painless, and both indicate reactive disease.
steps.tx: Skin hallmarks are **keratoderma blennorrhagicum** (hyperkeratotic pustular papules on palms and soles resembling pustular psoriasis) and **circinate balanitis** (painless serpiginous erosions of glans and coronal sulcus). Oral ulcers are small, shallow, and painless on tongue, hard palate, and buccal mucosa, often missed without deliberate inspection. Palmoplantar pustules with arthritis indicate reactive disease, while psoriasis-like nails without arthritis do not.

steps.say: Full dose NSAIDs open therapy with joint injections for stubborn joints. Systemic steroids are reserved for severe polyarticular flares. Most acute disease is settled within months. Chronicity beyond 3 to 6 months is the trigger for a new plan.
steps.tx: Acute therapy centres on full dose **NSAIDs** (anti-inflammatory painkillers). Intra-articular glucocorticoid injections rescue refractory mono or oligoarthritis, while systemic glucocorticoids are reserved for severe polyarticular flares or systemic inflammation. Most acute episodes settle within months. Arthritis persisting beyond **3 to 6 months** is chronic disease and requires DMARD escalation rather than further NSAID courses.

steps.say: Chlamydia requires antibiotics for the patient and all partners. Doxycycline at 100 mg twice daily over 7 days, or single dose azithromycin at 1 g, are the regimens. Post-dysenteric arthritis is unmoved by antibiotics. The joint and the germ are treated on separate tracks.
steps.tx: A positive **Chlamydia** trachomatis nucleic acid test from first void urine or cervical swab sets two tracks running: **doxycycline 100 mg** taken twice daily across **7 days**, or single dose **azithromycin 1 g**, for the patient plus all sexual partners, alongside anti-inflammatory joint therapy. Germ killing never shortens post-dysenteric enteric arthritis, so the joint track runs its own course. Untreated partners guarantee reinfection.

steps.say: Chronic peripheral arthritis beyond 6 months requires sulfasalazine 2 to 3 g daily. Anti TNF biologics are the rescue for refractory cases. This stage is reached by 15 to 20 percent of patients. This figure is the map of the wider spondyloarthritis family.
steps.tx: Chronic reactive arthritis affects **15 to 20 percent** of patients. **Sulfasalazine 2 g to 3 g** daily is the conventional DMARD of choice for chronic peripheral disease, with anti TNF biologics rescuing refractory cases. Achilles enthesitis, dactylitis, and alternating buttock pain mark patients drifting toward axial SpA criteria. Arthritis beyond 6 months without DMARD is undertreated disease.

vis.alt: Diverse axial, peripheral, and extra-articular manifestations of spondyloarthritis.
vis.caption: Reactive arthritis sits inside the spondyloarthritis family with shared skin, eye, and enthesis features. Chronic cases drift toward axial criteria. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Sterile arthritis after infection with urethritis and red eyes is reactive until proven otherwise. HLA-B27 is the predictor of the course while skin lesions are the confirmers. Full dose NSAIDs are the lead, injections are the rescue, and sulfasalazine holds chronic disease. Partners are treated whenever Chlamydia is found.
steps.tx: Sterile arthritis **1 to 4 weeks** after gut or genital infection, with urethritis and conjunctivitis, is reactive arthritis until proven otherwise. **HLA-B27** in **60 to 85 percent** predicts severity, keratoderma and circinate balanitis confirm it, and NAAT directs partner therapy. Full dose **NSAIDs** lead, intra-articular steroids rescue stubborn joints, and **sulfasalazine 2 g to 3 g** holds the **15 to 20 percent** who turn chronic.
